$comment: CORRECTION 2026-08-04 (adversarial re-review): the claim below that none of these vias sits under a
component courtyard is FALSE for TP2 (/+3V3). Its copper lapped 0.234 mm
into C34's courtyard, and worse, its mask aperture was 0.0295 mm from
C34's pad -- below the 0.100 mm minimum web, so the two merged into one
opening in the exported gerber. That is a solder-theft path into an MCU
rail decoupler, and DRC could not see it because both are on /+3V3 and
solder_mask_bridge only fires between different nets. TP2 moved to
(121.314,99.332) in U59. The claim was made by testing the via CENTRE
instead of its shape -- the exact error CLAUDE.md's window-query rule
exists to prevent, in the unit that cites it.
U53 -- give the power rails probe points. Review items 23/24 (dft).
WHAT THE FINDING ACTUALLY ASKED FOR. The DFT lens's complaint was about
bring-up diagnosis, not signal integrity: 'a powered healthy board looks
identical to a dead one' and 'no bare-copper +5 V probe point'. The first
question at power-up is whether the rails came up, and there was no way to
answer it without clipping onto a component lead.
An earlier revision of this file probed the centre-panel SPI bus instead
(SCLK/MOSI/MISO/CS), reasoning from the U9 clock-walk procedure's TP1-TP5.
That was inferred, not asked for, and it was the wrong target -- Kevin does
not want test pads on the screen bus. Retargeted 2026-08-03.
PARTLY REFUTING ITEM 24 FIRST: 'no bare ground reference' is not true.
MP1-MP4 are 5.00 x 5.00 mm bare-copper pads on /GND at the four board
corners (30,90), (30,130), (270,90), (270,130) -- mask open, no paste, and a
better ground target than any via. They are simply far from everything, so
the gap was a LOCAL ground next to whatever you are measuring.
NO NEW PARTS. Vias already exist on both rails with a /GND via between them,
so opening the mask over three of them buys the whole thing: no footprints,
no BOM line, no CPL row, no schematic symbol, nothing for schematic parity
to disagree with. The board default tents every via front and back, which
stays right for the other 231.
The three sit just west of U1, mid-board, none of them under a component
courtyard, and all clear of silkscreen -- so unlike the SPI attempt this
costs NO silk_over_copper warnings and the board stays at 0 violations at
--severity-all.
Why these two rails answer the question. /+5V is downstream of the
ideal-diode ORing, so it reads live whether the board is fed from the barrel
jack or USB -- it says 'input power reached the board'. /+3V3 is the buck's
output, so it says 'U3 is actually switching'. Together they separate a dead
supply from a dead regulator from a dead MCU, which is exactly the split you
cannot make by looking at an unlit board.
A 0.6 mm via is a small target: fine tip and a sprung ground lead, not an
alligator clip. For a bigger ground, MP1-MP4 are still there.
Not silk-labelled, because kicad_handroute.py has no silk-text operation --
the same gap that blocks review items 26 and 27. Until that exists these
three are identified by coordinate here and in the triage doc, and by eye as
the only bare copper in that area.

steps.step: 1/1  open the mask over three vias -> +5V, +3V3 and a local ground
